raw_response:
*Reasoning in my own voice:*

I'm 76 now, been farming this land for over fifty years. My wife and I run these 21.4 mu ourselves — our son works in the city, comes back maybe twice a year. Labor is my biggest worry these days. My back isn't what it was, so I've had to think carefully about what I can still handle.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October, about 13 mu. It's mid-April now, the wheat is at jointing — I need to topdress and give it spring water soon. The same 13 mu will go to maize right after I harvest the wheat in early June. That turnaround is tight, maybe 5-7 days, and I'll hire the combine and the no-till planter from the village cooperative like I do every year. Can't handle that alone anymore.

I keep 6 mu in cotton on the western plot — that soil is a bit saltier, cotton does better there than grain. Cotton picking in September-October is the killer; I pay my niece's family to help with the picking, costs me more each year. But the price has been decent and I know cotton. Fifty-five years of it.

The 2.4 mu of chili is my cash crop. My wife manages most of it honestly — she's better with the transplanting and staking. We sell fresh to the buyer who comes through the village. It's a lot of water and labor for a small plot but it pays.

For fertilizer — I usually do about 15-17 kg of urea per mu on wheat, split between base in October and topdress now. That's what the extension fellow suggested years ago and it's worked well enough. I don't change much year to year. If I see the wheat looking pale I'll add a bit more at jointing, but this year it looks good. Maize gets similar, mostly base with a topdress at the big-trumpet stage. Cotton needs less nitrogen, maybe 12-13 kg, but more potassium for the bolls. Chili is greedy — I put down a lot of compost in winter plus chemical fertilizer through the season.

Irrigation I'm careful with. The well is deep and the electricity cost keeps creeping up. Wheat gets three waterings — overwintering done, jointing this week, then flowering. Maize maybe one or two if June-July is dry. Cotton one or two. Chili needs regular water, every 10 days or so in summer.

I'm not trying to break any yield records. I'm trying to have a steady year, no surprises, enough grain for us and some cash from cotton and chili to cover the year's expenses and keep something aside. At my age that's what matters.
